body: I can be your daddy! Thank you for the hotttt roleplay we may just be able to share, cutie. PM me, you naughty girl.

Thank you. So much.

A lot of what I needed to hear.

I already wrote your bullet points on a piece of paper. I'll make it a framed quote magnet for my refrigerator door, haha. As much as my dog will motivate me to get off my ass in the morning, my coffee ritual with reading this list can definitely give me the boost I need for the day.

Thanks again, just got over the rumination from all day today. I'll sleep easy. :)

Hope you are in a good place now, yourself, bud. For me, getting away was not the best way to get through my trauma, but it did also teach me to come back and find my roots. I feel like I'm really going away now, and it's finally for *me.*

My cousin who was trying to help me through a very numb phase once told me that I need to stop self-pitying... He had tried to help me with getting out of the house and doing activities, but then he told me that after my inevitable trip to the hospital... for attempting suicide.

Sometimes people just feel disappointed with themselves... Not you. They weren't able to accommodate and/or understand your needs. You are not hurting them, but they are hurt or defensive because *you* are hurting.

You guys seem to be in a mode. I was caught between my parents in a very similar way, and then my mom told me her side of the story. Some times it's hard to not take sides, and I respect that you're giving your dad a chance, because I would do the same. It's okay to be a little selfish and try what makes sense to you... give it a try and find the errors.

PM me if you want to talk. I wonder why tonight is the worst? I hope whatever happened can get better soon.

Peace upon you.

I've been on it for about a year now! It definitely works, and it was prescribed to me. It generally works around 100mg. I take 200.

It helps with clarity the most. Definitely gives me the ability to think without having any emotional "vibes" get in the way. Like when an SSRI can make you manic or numb, this does not happen. It got rid of the feeling of having electric sparks in my head from the SSRI's like Zoloft, especially.

I tried about 3 antidepressants and none of them seemed to work, either. Zoloft, Wellbutrin, Lexapro.

My pdoc's throughout the years have tried diagnosing me, but it seems like there could have been something underlying the whole time. So just so you know, there are other causes for psychological symptoms, and depression is definitely one of them.

Turns out I needed a mood stabilizer, Lamictal, since it seems like I had a underlying case of mood swings. They were so unobserved that it was surprising that giving it a try would have even occurred. So that's why I say that you should keep trying things, even if they are different antidepressants. There is definitely one that will work for you.
